subject: English
central_question: How does Horace Danby’s confidence and selective dishonesty allow a clever thief to exploit his trust and turn his careful plan against him?
in_scope_units: Read and Find Out: Horace Danby’s respectable life, love of rare books, and yearly robberies
His detailed preparation for robbing Shotover Grange, including the safe, alarm, key, dog, and hay fever
Read and Find Out: the young woman’s appearance, authority, and claim to be the lady of the house
The conversation in which she studies Horace’s fear of prison and persuades him to open the safe
The fingerprints, arrest, real owner, prison library, and rejection of “honour among thieves”
Glossary vocabulary connected with hay fever
Think about it: clues, deception, Horace’s mixed character, and failure of planning
Talk about it: punishment, intentions, honesty, and whether ends justify means
Suggested reading connected with crime and unexpected reversals

known_pitfalls.claim: The young woman in red is the owner’s wife.
known_pitfalls.correction: She is another thief who pretends to be the lady of the house and tricks Horace into opening the safe.
He robs one safe every year to finance his collection of rare and expensive books.
He removes his gloves to light the woman’s cigarette and later opens the safe without them, leaving fingerprints all over the room.

known_pitfalls.claim: Horace is innocent of the Shotover Grange robbery.
known_pitfalls.correction: He does not keep the jewels, but he illegally enters the house and opens the safe; his own actions make the theft possible.

known_pitfalls.claim: The story supports the saying “honour among thieves.”
known_pitfalls.correction: The woman deceives another thief, and Horace becomes angry whenever the saying is mentioned.

recommended_example_progression: Begin with the first Read and Find Out questions on Horace’s collection and motive for yearly theft.
Use the second Read and Find Out set to identify the speaker and the real culprit.
Use Think about it 2 to analyse the subtle methods by which the woman impersonates the owner.
Use Think about it 3 to explain why Horace is respectable but not completely honest.
Use Think about it 4 and Talk about it 2 to evaluate the failure of planning and the claim that good intentions justify wrong actions.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with Think about it questions 1–4 and Talk about it questions 1–2, followed by Suggested reading.
